t: 2171. Removing Minimum Number of Magic Beans
o: After removals, every non-empty bag holds the same value v, which must be one of the original bean counts. For a chosen target v, bags with fewer than v beans are emptied entirely and bags with more are trimmed to v, so removed = total - v * (number of bags with beans >= v). Sort beans and evaluate this for each distinct value as target; sorting ensures the suffix count is just n - i. Example 1: sorted [1,4,5,6], target 4 removes 1 + 0 + 1 + 2 = 4. Brute force over targets with a recount is O(n^2); sorting plus a linear scan is O(n log n).
k: The final common value must equal some existing beans[i].
Cost for target v = total - v * (count of bags >= v); after sorting, that count is n - i at position i.

a.i: Sort, then for each index i treat beans[i] as the target; the kept amount is beans[i] * (n - i) and everything else is removed.
s: Sort beans and compute the total.
For each i, candidate cost = total - beans[i] * (n - i).
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting dominates; the scan is linear

a.i: Bean values are bounded by 1e5, so bucket counts and sweep targets from high to low, maintaining the suffix count of bags >= v — avoiding the sort entirely.
s: Bucket-count each bean value up to M = max(beans).
Sweep v from M down to 1, accumulating suffix count sc of bags with beans >= v.
Candidate cost = total - v * sc; return the minimum.
a.t: O(n + M) — bucket fill plus a sweep over values up to the maximum

w: Use 64-bit accumulation: totals reach 1e10. Duplicate targets are harmless (they give the same cost). Pitfall: forgetting that smaller bags are emptied completely rather than trimmed — the formula total - v*sc encodes this automatically. Follow-up: what if emptied bags were disallowed — then only targets <= min matter.
